draft.title: The traditional view of consumers
card: Traditional economics makes assumptions about how consumers behave. These assumptions let economists predict choices with simple models.
consumers act to benefit themselves and their own household, rather than to help others or the economy.
consumers choose sensibly, using full and accurate information about prices, quality and alternatives.
the satisfaction a consumer gets from a good or service. Consumers try to get the most utility they can from what they spend.
draft.remember: The traditional consumer is self-interested, rational and well informed, and aims for the most utility.

a.q: Which describes the traditional view of a consumer buying a phone?
opts: They compare all models and pick the one with most utility
They pick the model most popular with friends and family
They pick the cheapest model, whatever it can do
They pick a model after seeing one advertisement for it
a.why: The traditional consumer is well informed and rational, so they compare the alternatives and choose the one that gives the most utility. Choosing the cheapest is tempting, but the aim is satisfaction, not the lowest price.
a.clue: Think about information and the aim of the purchase.

b.q: Priya has $60 to spend on lunch in Geelong. A traditional economist assumes she will do which of these?
opts: Spend it where she expects the most satisfaction for herself
Spend it where it helps the most local café owners
Spend it on whatever her friends buy that day
Spend it on the item with the highest price
b.why: The traditional view says consumers act in their own interest and try to get the most utility from their spending. Helping café owners puts others first, which the view does not assume. Following friends is not a rational comparison of utility.
b.clue: Whose benefit does the traditional consumer put first?

a.best: They compare all models and pick the one with most utility

b.best: Spend it where she expects the most satisfaction for herself
